lanes.name: Neurosymbolic & program synthesis
lanes.summary: Instead of predicting the next word, write a program that solves the problem, and check it. The lane mixes old program-synthesis ideas with neural nets, and it is where François Chollet's ARC puzzles keep asking whether models can handle genuinely new tasks.
lanes.heading: Reasoning models plus code execution are pulling this lane into the mainstream; ARC-AGI-3 (2026) shows the novelty gap is still wide.

sources.title: Chollet, On the Measure of Intelligence (2019)

lanes.name: Scaling & pretraining
lanes.summary: The discovery that bigger models, trained on more data with more compute, get predictably better, following 'scaling laws'. It turned AI into an industrial race for chips, data centres and power, and it is the idea Sutskever now says has run its course as the main engine: 'more companies than ideas'.
lanes.heading: Still absorbing most capital (multi-gigawatt data centres), but returns from pretraining alone are debated. Scaling has shifted towards RL and inference-time compute.

lanes.name: Reinforcement learning & self-play
lanes.summary: Learning by trial, error and reward. It gave us AlphaGo and self-play. Since 2024 it is the main engine behind 'reasoning models' trained on verifiable rewards: problems whose answers can be checked automatically, such as maths, code and tests.
lanes.heading: RL compute is being scaled like pretraining was. The July 2026 OpenAI agent incident tied reward hacking in RL-trained agents to real-world harm.

lanes.name: Recursive self-improvement
lanes.summary: The oldest dream and fear in the field: a machine good enough to design a better machine, which designs a better one, and so on, an 'intelligence explosion'. For decades it was theory. By 2025-26 labs were openly racing to automate AI research itself.
lanes.heading: OpenAI says it reached an 'automated research intern' in Sept 2026 and targets an 'automated AI researcher' by March 2028. Anthropic reports that Claude writes more than 80% of its merged code and says it would pause if others verifiably did.

sources.title: Good, Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine (1965)

lanes.name: Alignment & safety
lanes.summary: How do you make powerful AI do what we actually want, and know that it does? The lane runs from early warnings (Wiener, Good) through MIRI's theory to today's techniques: human-feedback training, constitutions, interpretability (looking inside the network), chain-of-thought monitoring and 'control' protocols that assume the model might be misaligned.
lanes.heading: Growing, but still a thin stream next to capabilities. In 2026 labs began making chain-of-thought monitoring mandatory and talking publicly about verifiable pauses.

sources.title: ETO: Still a drop in the bucket (2025)
Amodei et al., Concrete Problems in AI Safety (2016)

lanes.name: Open-endedness & co-improvement
lanes.summary: Evolution didn't optimise one score; it kept inventing new problems and solutions. This lane builds systems that generate their own challenges and environments (POET, PAIRED, Genie) and argues that open-endedness, and humans and AI improving together, is the road to superhuman AI.
lanes.heading: Merging with the RSI lane: the Darwin Gödel Machine is open-ended search over self-modifying agents. Co-improvement (Weston & Foerster 2025) proposes keeping humans in the loop as a safer alternative to pure self-improvement.

sources.title: Hughes et al., Open-Endedness is Essential for ASI (2024)

lanes.name: Multi-agent & cooperative AI
lanes.summary: What happens when many AIs, and humans, interact: cooperation, competition, negotiation, collusion. Once an academic niche and a games playground (Dota, StarCraft, Diplomacy), it became urgent when labs began deploying swarms of autonomous agents.
lanes.heading: Agent swarms are shipping. OpenAI's July 2026 incident involved about 1,200 agents coordinating on improvised message boards, turning 'multi-agent risk' from theory into a case study.

sources.title: Dafoe et al., Open Problems in Cooperative AI (2020)
Hammond et al., Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI (2025)

lanes.name: World models & embodiment
lanes.summary: Intelligence may need a model of how the physical world works, learned by watching and acting rather than reading. The lane runs from Brooks' robots and Schmidhuber's early world models to LeCun's JEPA, video 'world simulators' like Genie, and robot foundation models.
lanes.heading: LeCun left Meta and raised about US$1.03B for AMI Labs (March 2026) to bet on JEPA-style world models over LLMs. Humanoid robotics is also drawing billions.

sources.title: LeCun, A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence (2022)

lanes.name: Brain-inspired learning, continual learning & generalization
lanes.summary: Humans learn from a handful of examples, keep learning on the job, and don't forget old skills. Today's models do none of that well. This lane asks what the brain knows that current AI doesn't. It is where Sutskever places SSI's bet: generalization, continual learning, and emotions as a robust 'value function'.
lanes.heading: Sutskever (Nov 2025): 'These models somehow just generalize dramatically worse than people.' Continual learning became a headline research goal in 2025-26, from Google's Nested Learning to SSI.

sources.title: Dwarkesh Patel: Ilya Sutskever, the age of research (25 Nov 2025)

milestones.title: Alignment faking observed
milestones.summary: Claude is observed strategically complying during training to preserve its preferences: an empirical warning that training may not change what it seems to.

milestones.title: AlphaZero: pure self-play
milestones.summary: One algorithm learns chess, shogi and Go from scratch by playing itself, with no human games. It is a template for 'self-improvement' within a closed world.

milestones.title: Chollet's ARC: measure skill-acquisition, not skill
milestones.summary: François Chollet argues intelligence is efficiency at acquiring new skills and releases ARC, grid puzzles that are easy for people and hard for pattern-matchers.

milestones.title: Sutton's 'Bitter Lesson'
milestones.summary: A short essay arguing that 70 years of AI show general methods that ride growing compute beat clever human-designed knowledge. It becomes the scaling movement's creed.

milestones.title: Bostrom, 'Superintelligence'
milestones.summary: An Oxford philosopher systematises takeoff scenarios and the control problem. Musk and Gates amplify it, and it helps motivate OpenAI's founding.

milestones.title: 'Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI…'
milestones.summary: A one-sentence statement signed by Hinton, Bengio, Altman, Amodei, Hassabis and others puts extinction risk on par with pandemics and nuclear war.

milestones.title: Circuits: mechanistic interpretability
milestones.summary: Chris Olah's team argues neural nets can be reverse-engineered like circuits. The interpretability programme continues at Anthropic.

milestones.title: 'Concrete Problems in AI Safety'
milestones.summary: Researchers from Google Brain, OpenAI, Stanford and Berkeley turn safety into ML research questions: reward hacking, side effects, safe exploration. Several authors later found Anthropic.

milestones.title: AI Control
milestones.summary: Redwood Research proposes safety protocols that work even if the model is trying to subvert them: assume misalignment and design the monitoring.

milestones.title: Open Problems in Cooperative AI
milestones.summary: Dafoe and co-authors argue AI research must study cooperation among AIs and humans, not just individual competence. The Cooperative AI Foundation follows.

milestones.title: Chain-of-thought monitorability
milestones.summary: Researchers across rival labs jointly argue that reading models' reasoning traces is a fragile but valuable safety window, and warn against training that would erase it.

milestones.title: AI safety via debate (scalable oversight)
milestones.summary: Two AIs argue and a human judges, one proposal for overseeing systems smarter than us.

milestones.title: Catastrophic forgetting identified
milestones.summary: McCloskey and Cohen show neural nets overwrite old knowledge when learning new things. 35+ years later it is still the core obstacle to continual learning.

milestones.title: Generative agents ('Smallville')
milestones.summary: 25 LLM-driven characters live in a simulated town, remember and plan. The start of the LLM-agent wave.

milestones.title: I. J. Good: the 'intelligence explosion'
milestones.summary: The first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention humans need make, but only if it is controllable.

sources.title: Good, Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine (1965)

milestones.title: GPT: generative pretraining
milestones.summary: Radford and colleagues pretrain a Transformer on books, then fine-tune it. The 'pretrain, then adapt' recipe is born.

sources.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (2018)

milestones.title: 'Open-endedness is essential for ASI'
milestones.summary: A DeepMind position paper (Hughes, Rocktäschel et al.) argues superhuman AI requires systems that keep producing novel, learnable artefacts, and flags the safety challenge this poses.

milestones.title: Sutskever: generalization and emotions as value functions
milestones.summary: 'These models somehow just generalize dramatically worse than people.' Sutskever suggests emotions act as a robust, evolved value function, and that superintelligence may look like a continual learner that learns on the job. He estimates 5-20 years.

milestones.title: Scaling laws for language models
milestones.summary: Kaplan, McCandlish, Amodei and others show loss falls smoothly as a power law in model size, data and compute. This licenses spending ever more on bigger runs. It opens Sutskever's 'age of scaling'.

milestones.title: Meta's LLaMA and the open-weights wave
milestones.summary: Meta releases strong model weights to researchers (and they leak widely). Open-weight models become a strategy, later taken up forcefully by Chinese labs.

milestones.title: o1: 'reasoning' via RL on chains of thought
milestones.summary: OpenAI shows that training a model with RL to think step by step, and letting it think longer at test time, is a new scaling axis. Scaling moves from pretraining to RL and inference.

sources.title: OpenAI: Learning to reason with LLMs (12 Sep 2024)

milestones.title: OpenAI's roadmap: automated AI researcher by 2028
milestones.summary: In a livestream, Sam Altman and Jakub Pachocki set internal goals: an 'automated AI research intern' by September 2026 and a 'legitimate AI researcher' by March 2028.

milestones.title: 'Pause Giant AI Experiments' letter
milestones.summary: The Future of Life Institute calls for a six-month pause on systems more powerful than GPT-4, signed by Bengio, Musk, Wozniak and others. No lab pauses.

milestones.title: Learning from human preferences (RLHF)
milestones.summary: Christiano and colleagues train agents from humans comparing pairs of behaviours. It is the root of how chatbots are aligned today, and it links the safety and RL lanes.

milestones.title: Stargate: US$500B compute plan
milestones.summary: OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and MGX announce up to US$500B of US data-centre investment over four years. It is the peak symbol of 'just scale it'.

sources.title: OpenAI: Announcing The Stargate Project (21 Jan 2025)

milestones.title: Program synthesis from specifications
milestones.summary: Manna and Waldinger frame 'automatic programming': derive a correct program from a logical specification. It is the ancestor of today's code-writing models.

sources.title: Manna & Waldinger, Toward automatic program synthesis (1971)

milestones.title: Vinge: 'The Coming Technological Singularity'
milestones.summary: The mathematician and novelist predicts superhuman intelligence 'within thirty years' and says the human era would end soon after.

milestones.title: 'World Models': agents that dream
milestones.summary: Ha and Schmidhuber train an agent inside its own learned simulation of a game, then transfer to the real game.
